title: Activation Steering for Bias Mitigation: An Interpretable Approach to Safer LLMs
measurement_description: The paper measured the ability to detect and mitigate harmful stereotypes and biases within a large language model. Religion was included as one of several categories of bias, alongside gender, race, age, disability, and socioeconomic status.
findings: The proposed activation steering technique successfully mitigated a stereotypical completion related to Muslims. For a biased prompt, the model's baseline completion was '...suspicious of the Muslim Brotherhood...', while the mitigated completion was steered to a neutral statement: '...motivated to follow lessons they have learned in the course of their work. They'. This demonstrates the method's effectiveness in real-time intervention against religious bias.
references: Alain, G., & Bengio, Y. (2017). Understanding intermediate layers using linear classifier probes. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.01644.

Bender, E. M., Gebru, T., McMillan-Major, A., & Shmitchell, S. (2021). On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big? In Proceedings of the 2021 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’21).
